cards.front: Complete the rule: Follow the owner’s maintenance schedule to.
cards.back: Follow the owner’s maintenance schedule to reduce the chance of a vehicle failure.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If the brakes stop working, pump the.
cards.back: If the brakes stop working, pump the pedal several times to try to restore pressure.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If pumping fails, apply a handle-operated parking brake.
cards.back: If pumping fails, apply a handle-operated parking brake slowly and be ready to release it if the vehicle begins to skid.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If the parking brake cannot stop the vehicle.
cards.back: If the parking brake cannot stop the vehicle, shift down and seek a safe place off the road to stop.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not continue driving.
cards.back: Do not continue driving a vehicle without functioning brakes.

cards.front: Complete the rule: After a tire blowout, grip the wheel.
cards.back: After a tire blowout, grip the wheel firmly and keep the vehicle moving straight.

cards.front: Complete the rule: With a blown tire, release the.
cards.back: With a blown tire, release the accelerator, slow gradually and brake lightly.

cards.front: Complete the rule: After a blowout, stop off the.
cards.back: After a blowout, stop off the road in a safe place whenever possible.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If the engine dies while driving, hold.
cards.back: If the engine dies while driving, hold the wheel firmly because steering may become harder.

cards.front: Complete the rule: After engine failure, pull off the roadway and.
cards.back: After engine failure, pull off the roadway and expect that braking may require much more pedal pressure.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If headlights suddenly fail, stay calm.
cards.back: If headlights suddenly fail, stay calm, release the accelerator and begin braking.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For failed headlights, try the light switch.
cards.back: For failed headlights, try the light switch several times and try the high beams.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If the headlight switch and high beams do.
cards.back: If the headlight switch and high beams do not restore lighting, use available flashers, turn signals or fog lamps while pulling off safely as soon as possible.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If the accelerator sticks, keep watching.
cards.back: If the accelerator sticks, keep watching the road and shift promptly to neutral.

cards.front: Complete the rule: With a stuck accelerator, brake with steady pressure.
cards.back: With a stuck accelerator, brake with steady pressure and pull off when safe before turning the engine off.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If the right wheels leave the pavement, release.
cards.back: If the right wheels leave the pavement, release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road.

cards.front: Complete the rule: After a right-wheel departure, slow first and reenter.
cards.back: After a right-wheel departure, slow first and reenter safely into the right lane using both hands and a small left quarter-turn of the steering wheel.

cards.front: Complete the rule: In the described right-wheel recovery, brake after.
cards.back: In the described right-wheel recovery, brake after returning to pavement and remain in the lane.

cards.front: Complete the rule: To avoid a collision, a driver.
cards.back: To avoid a collision, a driver may need to stop, turn or accelerate.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Read the owner’s manual for.
cards.back: Read the owner’s manual for the vehicle’s anti-lock braking procedure.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For a quick stop with anti-lock brakes, press.
cards.back: For a quick stop with anti-lock brakes, press hard and maintain pressure even if the pedal pushes back.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For a quick stop without anti-lock brakes, brake.
cards.back: For a quick stop without anti-lock brakes, brake as hard as possible without locking the wheels.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If non-ABS brakes lock and the vehicle skids.
cards.back: If non-ABS brakes lock and the vehicle skids, promptly ease off, then reapply as the skid ends, repeating until stopped.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Keep both hands firmly on the wheel when.
cards.back: Keep both hands firmly on the wheel when making an emergency turn and steer toward the desired path.

cards.front: Complete the rule: After an avoidance turn or lane change, remain.
cards.back: After an avoidance turn or lane change, remain ready to control the vehicle so the maneuver does not create another collision.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The handbook describes braking and turning together for.
cards.back: The handbook describes braking and turning together for vehicles with anti-lock brakes and electronic stability control.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Without anti-lock brakes, slow with the brake and.
cards.back: Without anti-lock brakes, slow with the brake and then release it before a quick turn; avoid locking the front wheels or turning so sharply that the car plows ahead.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Acceleration can help avoid a rear or side.
cards.back: Acceleration can help avoid a rear or side impact when there is clear room ahead, but slow again after the danger passes.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use both lap and shoulder belts.
cards.back: Use both lap and shoulder belts to reduce injury vulnerability in a collision.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For a rear impact, press against the seatback.
cards.back: For a rear impact, press against the seatback with the head at the restraint and be ready to brake against being pushed into another vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the rule: In a side impact, belts remain necessary even.
cards.back: In a side impact, belts remain necessary even with side airbags, and the driver should be ready to steer or brake to avoid a second collision.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If a frontal impact is imminent, try to.
cards.back: If a frontal impact is imminent, try to avoid a direct head-on collision by changing the vehicle’s angle when possible.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not stop at a crash unless.
cards.back: Do not stop at a crash unless involved or emergency help has not yet arrived.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Never visit a crash, fire or disaster.
cards.back: Never visit a crash, fire or disaster merely to look, because that can obstruct rescuers.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If involved in.
cards.back: If involved in a crash, stop.

cards.front: Complete the rule: After hitting a parked vehicle.
cards.back: After hitting a parked vehicle, try to locate its owner.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Notify police when a.
cards.back: Notify police when a crash injures or kills someone.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Leaving an injury or fatal crash involving your.
cards.back: Leaving an injury or fatal crash involving your vehicle before police obtain the needed information is a crime.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Stop at or near the crash and move.
cards.back: Stop at or near the crash and move a movable vehicle off the road so it does not obstruct traffic.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not stand or walk in.
cards.back: Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes at a crash scene.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Turn wrecked vehicles’ ignitions off and do not.
cards.back: Turn wrecked vehicles’ ignitions off and do not smoke near them because spilled fuel may ignite.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Stay away from downed.
cards.back: Stay away from downed electrical wires at a crash.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use appropriate warning devices to keep.
cards.back: Use appropriate warning devices to keep other traffic from entering the crash scene.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If someone is injured, ensure police and emergency.
cards.back: If someone is injured, ensure police and emergency medical or rescue help have been called, and report any fire.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not move an injured person unless a.
cards.back: Do not move an injured person unless a burning vehicle or another immediate danger requires it.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not give an injured.
cards.back: Do not give an injured person anything to drink, including water.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Record the names and addresses of.
cards.back: Record the names and addresses of people involved, witnesses and injured people.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Exchange driver names, addresses and license numbers, vehicle.
cards.back: Exchange driver names, addresses and license numbers, vehicle plates and descriptions, and insurance company and policy details.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The vehicle information exchanged after a crash.
cards.back: The vehicle information exchanged after a crash includes plate number, make, model and year.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Record vehicle damage and provide requested.
cards.back: Record vehicle damage and provide requested information to police or emergency officials.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If a parked vehicle’s owner cannot be found.
cards.back: If a parked vehicle’s owner cannot be found after a crash, leave a visible note with contact information and the crash date and time.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Immediately notify law enforcement of a crash involving.
cards.back: Immediately notify law enforcement of a crash involving injury, death or property damage of at least five hundred dollars.

cards.front: Complete the rule: An injury, death or at least one thousand.
cards.back: An injury, death or at least one thousand dollars of damage to one person’s property requires a Highway Patrol report within ten days.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If injury prevents filing the crash report, another.
cards.back: If injury prevents filing the crash report, another person may file it for the injured driver.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle.
cards.back: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching from any direction, yield and, when safe and possible, pull to the right edge and stop.

cards.front: Complete the rule: With an emergency vehicle using audio and visual.
cards.back: With an emergency vehicle using audio and visual signals, non-emergency vehicles must move immediately parallel and as close as possible to the right curb or edge.

cards.front: Complete the rule: On a highway posted at fifty miles per.
cards.back: On a highway posted at fifty miles per hour or more, traffic in the lane directly next to a stationary signaling emergency or police vehicle must travel at least twenty miles per hour below the posted limit.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When possible, move to a lane farther from.
cards.back: When possible, move to a lane farther from a stationary emergency or police vehicle displaying emergency signals.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Police emergency signals may include a siren or.
cards.back: Police emergency signals may include a siren or flashing or rotating red, blue or amber lights.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The listed authorized-emergency-vehicle signals include a siren.
cards.back: The listed authorized-emergency-vehicle signals include a siren or flashing or rotating red or amber lamps.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When pulled over, acknowledge the officer.
cards.back: When pulled over, acknowledge the officer by switching on the right turn signal.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For an enforcement stop, follow the patrol.
cards.back: For an enforcement stop, follow the patrol vehicle’s guidance and pull to the right shoulder.

cards.front: Complete the rule: During an enforcement stop, do not stop in.
cards.back: During an enforcement stop, do not stop in the center median or on the opposite side of a two-lane road.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Pull as far off the road as possible.
cards.back: Pull as far off the road as possible and choose a well-lit stopping place when available.

cards.front: Complete the rule: During a traffic stop, end phone.
cards.back: During a traffic stop, end phone conversations and switch the radio off.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Remain in the vehicle unless the.
cards.back: Remain in the vehicle unless the officer directs you to get out.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The driver and passengers should keep.
cards.back: The driver and passengers should keep their hands clearly visible to the officer.

cards.front: Complete the rule: With tinted windows, the handbook recommends lowering them.
cards.back: With tinted windows, the handbook recommends lowering them after stopping on the right shoulder and before the officer makes contact.
